description: Capability/deny-path translation expectations for the codex adapter. Every input block here is harness-neutral and identical, case for case, to the other translation/*.json files; only the expected blocks are harness-specific. Codex's sandbox is mode-based, not tool-based (grounded against codex-cli 0.154.0): every LOOM capability is read-shaped, so a translatable envelope is sandbox_mode read-only with an unattended approval policy of never; writable_roots and network_access are pinned to their no-widening values so a default drift upstream is visible. Codex's sandbox cannot express a per-path read deny — read-only mode leaves the whole filesystem readable — so an envelope carrying deny paths is capability_unsupported, never served with the globs silently ignored (the plan's own rule: a path a harness cannot deny is capability_unsupported).

expected.subject: bf
expected.notes: Codex's read-only mode emits no command alias; bf is retired and cannot be silently accepted as a bead-readonly capability.

expected.subject: br
expected.notes: Codex's read-only mode emits no command alias; br is retired and cannot be silently accepted as a bead-readonly capability.

Where claude-print has an explicit no-op row for docs-readonly, codex's table needs no special case: the read-only sandbox already grants exactly what docs-readonly asks, so every known read-shaped capability translates to the same settings.

expected.subject: web-fetch
expected.notes: The read-only sandbox blocks network. Every codex configuration that reaches the web — network_access under workspace-write, or a sandbox bypass — lifts the restriction for every command in the run, which is precisely the silent widening the envelope forbids, so web-fetch has no codex spelling.

expected.subject: deploy
expected.notes: A name outside the vocabulary entirely. The first unknown capability aborts the whole translation even when every other capability would have translated.

expected.subject: deny_paths
expected.notes: One deny path is enough to sink the envelope: codex offers no per-path read deny, so the glob could only be dropped, and dropping it is ignoring the brief's one unconditional instruction.

expected.subject: deny_paths
expected.notes: Every capability in this envelope is individually codex-servable, but the envelope as a whole is not: the deny paths cannot be expressed, so the strand fails fast with capability_unsupported instead of running with the globs unreadable-by-contract. A codex-mapped strand is servable only with an envelope whose deny_paths is empty — which is the envelope the Scenario 8 codex-mapped mock run must carry.

expected.subject: deny_paths
expected.notes: Codex refuses the envelope before any list translation: read-only mode cannot express even a duplicated per-path deny, so the whole envelope remains unsupported.
